name: Celtic revival

attributes.attribute: grew from ecology-led and heritage-led interests
ritual and artistic expression of Celtic interest
criticize the movements for weak scholarship
base for some claimed Celtic rituals
unlikely to wane in the near future

sources: Carr-Gomm, Philip. *The Druid Renaissance.* London: Thorsons, 1996.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The Celtic revival is a present-day movement. Over the last twenty-five years, many people have sought Celtic belief and myth. They wanted a faith tied to their ancestry, one that fit modern needs. Some pursued ecology. They saw in Celtic ideas about land a vision free of capitalism, aimed past it. Others read Celtic tales for women who act boldly. They took a feminist outlook. Still others hunted ties to a dreamed-of pagan past. Followers pick up books on Celtic topics and hear Celtic song. Some make trips they call pilgrimages to Celtic lands. Others join bands that perform rites said to come from Celtic lore. These people name themselves Druids, pagans, neopagans, Wiccans, or witches. None of this is fresh. The British order of Druids started a century back. In Ireland, the Celtic Twilight joined ritual with art. Revivalist practice has spread fast of late. Some academics mock these varied groups. Most members never read the old texts, and many forgo proper translation. Some beliefs they call old are new. Some rites come from Masonry, not from the Celts. Some hopeful social claims rest on no archaeology. Still, the revival will likely endure. If scholars soften toward the spiritual search, they will win a hearing. Practitioners, in turn, could ground their practices in real history.

okr.objective: The Celtic revival is a contemporary movement reviving Celtic spirituality and rituals.
key_results: The movement draws ecologists, feminists, and heritage seekers.
Seekers call themselves Druids, pagans, neopagans, Wiccans, or witches.
The British order of Druids and the Celtic Twilight are earlier roots.
Scholars criticize the revival for gaps in scholarship.
okr.evidence: Monaghan, Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore
